descriptionChirho: Piel stem of ארשׂ meaning 'to betroth, engage in marriage', used of the active party who contracts a betrothal. The Piel perfect 3ms appears in Deut 20:7 (אֵרַשׂ 'has betrothed a wife'), Piel perfect 1cs in 2 Sam 3:14 (David: אֵרַשְׂתִּי 'I betrothed'), Piel imperfect 2ms in Deut 28:30 (תְאָרֵשׂ 'you shall betroth a wife'), and Piel conjunctive perfect 1cs with 2fs suffix in Hos 2:19-20 (three-fold וְאֵרַשְׂתִּיךְ 'I will betroth you', God's covenant promise to Israel). Multilingual glosses are consistent: arb خطب 'to betroth', deu 'verloben', fra 'fiancer', hin मंगनी करना, kor 약혼하다/약혼시키다, spa 'desposar'.

Pual (passive) stem of ארשׂ meaning 'to be betrothed, be engaged', describing the woman's status as one who has been betrothed to a man. Attested as Pual perfect 3fs (אֹרָשָׂה) in Exod 22:16, Deut 22:28, and as Pual participle feminine (מְאֹרָשָׂה / הַמְאֹרָשָׂה) in Deut 22:23, 22:25, 22:27, all in legal contexts defining the status and rights of a betrothed woman. Glosses show passive meaning: arb مخطوبة 'betrothed (f.)', deu/eng 'betrothed/is-betrothed', hin मंगनी हुई 'betrothal-occurred', kor 약혼된 'betrothed', spa 'desposada'. The Pual passive sense is lexicographically distinct from the active Piel betrothing.
